extractions.description: This paper introduces the concept of forget-and-relearn as a beneficial paradigm for machine learning, particularly in shaping learning trajectories of deep neural networks. It argues that forgetting can lead to the generalization of models by selectively removing undesirable information, followed by relearning to reinforce consistently useful features. The paper provides evidence and theoretical groundwork for this paradigm, proposing targeted forgetting operations to improve existing iterative training algorithms.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on the machine learning paradigm of forget-and-relearn and discusses its implications for neural networks and algorithmic improvements. It does not address climate change or any related environmental themes.
climate_change_is_central.quote: In this work, we study a general learning paradigm that we refer to as forget-and-relearn, and show that forgetting can also benefit learning in artificial neural networks.
